newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Moscow's top educator hurt in assassination bid.
newsitem.headline: Moscow's top educator hurt in assassination bid.

text.p: The Moscow city government's top education official was wounded by gunfire to the head in an assassination attempt, police said on Tuesday.

In the Moscow attack, a gunman fired at Lyubov Kezina, 50 and who heads the capital's education committee, on Monday evening as she sat in her government car, police said. She suffered a surface wound to the head and was taken to hospital.

Police said her attempt to introduce a new system of examinations might have prompted the attack, although Russian Public Television reported the motive could be related to the allocation of school construction funds.
With Russia's legal system still largely ineffective, many disputes are settled with a bullet to the head rather than a petition to the court.

In an unrelated incident, police in Volgograd in southern Russia said a conscript accidently launched a signal rocket at a military induction center. Two women were wounded from shattered glass, a police duty officer said.
